title: Philippine real estate transaction and estate tax reference
scope: Illustrative orientation for Batangas residential and vacant-land transactions.
authorityNote: Statutory rates published by the BIR, the Registry of Deeds, the LGU and the National Treasury. Rates are reproduced here for orientation only. The BIR and the LGU determine the actual amounts payable, and any figure in this file may be superseded by a later circular or statute.
taxBaseNote: For the illustrated qualifying capital-asset sale, CGT uses the higher of selling price and statutory fair market value; statutory FMV considers the BIR zonal reference and assessor schedule values. Without an entered price, the planning estimate is an assumed selling price, not statutory FMV. Missing assessor values, asset classification and exemptions must be confirmed. There is no 50%-of-zonal proxy or excess-only CGT in this model.

transaction.label: Capital gains tax
transaction.note: 6% of the higher applicable gross selling price or statutory FMV for qualifying capital-asset real property. Ordinary-asset sales and exemptions require a different assessment.
transaction.deadlineFrom: date of notarisation of the deed of sale
transaction.penalty: Surcharge and interest depend on taxpayer classification and circumstances; confirm current BIR rules

transaction.label: Documentary stamp tax
transaction.legalBasis: Sec. 196 NIRC; filing under Sec. 200(B), as amended by RA 11976 Sec. 30
transaction.note: 1.5% planning approximation; the statutory document calculation and applicable exemptions must be checked. General filing deadline is 10 days after the close of the month the taxable document was made, signed, issued, accepted or transferred, subject to applicable rules.
transaction.deadlineFrom: close of the month the taxable document was made, signed, issued, accepted or transferred
transaction.penalty: Surcharge and interest depend on taxpayer classification and circumstances; confirm current BIR rules

transaction.label: Local transfer tax
transaction.note: 0.5% is an illustrative provincial rate. Cities may impose up to 50% more under Sec. 151 (up to 0.75%); verify the relevant LGU ordinance and valuation basis.
transaction.deadlineFrom: date of the deed of transfer
transaction.penalty: Interest and penalties fixed by local ordinance

transaction.label: Registration fee (estimate)
transaction.note: An approximation for orientation. The Registry of Deeds computes the fee from its own schedule, which includes a minimum and is not a flat percentage.

transaction.label: Notarial fee (estimate)
transaction.legalBasis: Quoted professional fee; no universal amount assumed
transaction.note: Not supplied and excluded by default. Obtain a written quote; fees may depend on the act and agreement.

transaction.label: Broker's commission
transaction.note: Illustrative negotiated 3% to 5% of the agreed price, assumed seller-paid here; confirm rate and allocation in writing.

estate.grossEstateBasis: The value of the estate at the time of death, typically the BIR zonal value or the market value, whichever the BIR accepts.
estate.standardDeductionBasis: Sec. 86(A)(1) NIRC, as amended by RA 10963 Sec. 23 (citizen/resident estate)
estate.taxBasis: Secs. 84 and 86 NIRC, as amended by RA 10963 Secs. 22-23: 6% of net taxable estate
estate.penalty: Surcharge and interest depend on circumstances; confirm current BIR rules
estate.deadlineFrom: date of death (one calendar year, not always exactly 365 days)
estate.note: These property-only scenarios assume the property were the entire citizen/resident estate. Actual liability requires all estate assets, applicable death-date values, liabilities and deductions. The PHP 10M family-home limit is conditional, not an additional universal exemption. Registrable property may require an estate return even when estimated tax is zero.

steps.deadline: Generally within 10 days after the close of the document month; confirm applicable rules
